panels.figure_caption: Vasculitis on Ear Rash on the left ear showed retiform purpura with few hemorrhagic bullae. No hand, foot, or other facial involvement was reported. This ear rash is a hallmark of levamisole-associated vasculitis.
in_text_mentions: ent was discharged on empiric antibiotic treatment for presumed otitis media. The patient represented to care two days later with worsening purpuric and tender rash which had spread to his left upper extremity and bilateral lower extremities (Figures 1, 2). He stated he had a similar rash approximately one year prior which resolved without medical intervention. The rash also showed no signs of blanching. The leading differential diagnosis became a vasculitis of unknown etiology, possibly rheumatoid arthritis given the history of autoimmune disease, and the patient was discharged on prednisone.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of lower leg showing large ulcerative lesion. Disease attribution supported by disease-focused article title 'The Ulcerative Effects of Levamisole-Induced Vasculitis' together with specific captioned manifestation and in-text ulcerative lesions with necrotic centers in context of cocaine use and c-ANCA-positive vasculitis.
panels.attribution_text: Zavaro et al. The Ulcerative Effects of Levamisole-Induced Vasculitis.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.90012. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: ry of HIV, hepatitis C virus, deep vein thrombosis, syphilis, c-ANCA-positive vasculitis, and polysubstance abuse, specifically cocaine and fentanyl. A physical examination revealed a systolic murmur on a cardiovascular assessment and poor dentition with multiple missing teeth. Examination of the extremities demonstrated wound dressings saturated with purulent yellow drainage. Dermatologic inspection revealed ulcerative lesions on the lower extremities with necrotic centers and hypopigmented lesions (Figures 1, 2). The patient denied any pain, burning, itching, fevers, chills, or night sweats.

plate_findings.evidence: bilateral scarlet-colored purpura that was contiguous and non-blanching (Figure 1). It covered his inner thighs

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Caption 'Levamisole-induced vasculitis' panels A-D with purpuric lesions; in-text describes contiguous non-blanching scarlet purpura of inner thighs matching visual retiform purpura in panel A. B: Caption attributes panels to levamisole-induced vasculitis; visual shows scattered purpuric violaceous lesions down leg consistent with retiform purpura of extremities. C: Same disease attribution as panels A-B; large confluent scarlet to deep purple non-blanching purpura of thigh/leg typical of levamisole vasculopathy retiform purpura. D: Caption includes panel D as levamisole-induced vasculitis lesion on flank; in-text notes purpura covered left flank; morphology is purpuric retiform plaque, vocabulary has only extremity retiform purpura term so coded by morphology with trunk site in proposed term.
panels.attribution_text: Latif et al. Levamisole-induced Vasculitis in a Hepatitis C Patient: A General Medicine Ward Perspective on Diagnosis and Management.. Cureus 2019. doi:10.7759/cureus.5198. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Levamisole-induced vasculitis in a cocaine user. Images obtained one week after cocaine use. Black arrows pointing to lesions scattered across his body shown in panels A, B, C, and D.
in_text_mentions: saturation was 97% on room air. The physical exam was significant for coarse breath sounds bilaterally. He was coughing throughout the exam, with a small amount of bloody sputum production. He had bilateral scarlet-colored purpura that was contiguous and non-blanching (Figure 1). It covered his inner thighs and left flank. The purpura extended down both thighs, with deep purple lesions scattered throughout. Lesions were not raised, no skin breakdown could be appreciated, and some lesions were surrounded by hyperpigmented rings. He had mild erythema across the anterior abdomen and right flank.
